newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ details new approach to monetary projections.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ details new approach to monetary projections.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand said on Thursday its monetary policy statement due on June 27 would no longer assume nominal interest rates and the exchange rate to be constant.

"Instead the statement will show inflation returning to near the middle of the 0-3 percent target range and a path for how monetary conditions may need to evolve to achieve this," the bank said in a statement.
It said the change arose because for the first time it was using a new model of the New Zealand economy to produce projections underlying the statement.

"It is important to note that this change in presentation...does not inherently provide new information about our judegments of the extent of inflation pressures. It simple makes the potential implications for future monetary conditions The bank said it would continue to use a monetary conditions index as a guide to signalling its intentions, with the same 2:1 ratio of a 100 basis point move in the 90 day rate having about the same impact on aggregate demand as a two percent rise or fall in the Trade Weighted Index.
